lesson.intro: A conjunction is a joining word. It joins two words or two sentences together.
points: [[and]] adds more: I have a cat and a dog.
[[but]] shows a difference: I like durian but my sister does not.
[[or]] gives a choice: Do you want tea or coffee?
[[because]] gives a reason: She was late because it rained.
[[so]] shows a result: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
More joining words: before, after, until, while, when, although, unless.

examples.text: Would you like to draw [[or]] read?
We stayed at home [[because]] it was very hot.
[[Although]] it was raining, they played football.

questions.prompt: Which word is a conjunction (a joining word)?
Which word is a conjunction?
Which word joins the two ideas?
questions.sentence: I am tired but happy.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction gives a reason?
Which conjunction gives a choice?
Which conjunction shows a result?
Choose the best sentence.
options: I was thirsty, so I drank some water.
I was thirsty, but I drank some water.
I was thirsty, or I drank some water.
I was thirsty, because I drank some water.
questions.answer: I was thirsty, so I drank some water.
questions.explanation: Drinking water is the result of being thirsty.

questions.prompt: Join the sentences: "It was late. We went home."
options: It was late, so we went home.
It was late, but we went home.
It was late, or we went home.
It was late, unless we went home.
questions.answer: It was late, so we went home.

questions.prompt: Join the sentences: "She was ill. She went to school."
options: Although she was ill, she went to school.
Because she was ill, she went to school.
Unless she was ill, she went to school.
So she was ill, she went to school.
questions.answer: Although she was ill, she went to school.
questions.explanation: Going to school when ill is surprising, so we use "although".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: I have a pen but a pencil.
questions.explanation: "but" should be "and". We are adding another thing, so we use "and".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: It was cold, because I wore a jacket.
questions.explanation: "because" should be "so". Wearing a jacket is the result of the cold.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: I wanted to play, so it was raining.
questions.explanation: "so" should be "but". The rain is a problem, so we use "but".

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: She cried so she fell down.
questions.explanation: "so" should be "because". Falling down is the reason she cried.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Brush your teeth after you go to bed.
questions.explanation: "after" should be "before". We brush our teeth before going to bed.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: Although the test was easy, everyone passed.
questions.explanation: "Although" should be "Because". The easy test is the reason everyone passed.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
questions.sentence: I will call you unless I reach home.
questions.explanation: "unless" should be "when". The call happens at the time I reach home.
